## Savara Informed That FDA Will Not Take Action on the Molgramostim BLA for Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (Autoimmune PAP) by the PDUFA Date


November 20, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/999407632/files/doc_news/Savara-Informed-That-FDA-Will-Not-Take-Action-on-the-Molgramostim-BLA-for-Autoimmune-Pulmonary-Alveolar-Proteinosis-Autoimmune-PAP-by-GAT7H.pdf)


*No Revised Action Date Communicated by the FDA*


YARDLEY, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Savara Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fsavarapharma.com%2F&esheet=54644507&newsitemid=20261120300122&lan=en-US&anchor=Savara+Inc.&index=1&md5=cf81a4feb94bf683b6c96f9f4ac5eebb) (Nasdaq: SVRA), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has communicated that it will not meet the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of November 22, 2026 for the Company’s molgramostim inhalation solution (molgramostim) Biologics License Application (BLA) for the treatment of autoimmune PAP. The review of the BLA is ongoing and no revised action date has been provided by the agency.


“We appreciate the FDA’s continued efforts on our application and look forward to working closely with the agency to complete its review,” said Matt Pauls, J.D., M.B.A., Chair and Chief Executive Officer, Savara.


**About Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (Autoimmune PAP)**


Autoimmune PAP is a rare lung disease characterized by the abnormal build-up of surfactant in the alveoli. Surfactant consists of proteins and lipids and is an important physiological substance that lines the alveoli to prevent them from collapsing. In a healthy lung, excess surfactant is cleared and digested by immune cells called alveolar macrophages. Alveolar macrophages need to be stimulated by granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) to function properly in clearing surfactant, but in autoimmune PAP, GM-CSF is neutralized by autoantibodies against GM-CSF, rendering macrophages unable to adequately clear surfactant. As a result, an excess of surfactant accumulates in the alveoli, causing impaired gas transfer, resulting in clinical symptoms of shortness of breath, often with cough and frequent fatigue. Patients may also experience episodes of fever, chest pain, or coughing up blood, especially if secondary lung infection develops. In the long term, the disease can lead to serious complications, including lung fibrosis and the need for a lung transplant.


**About Molgramostim**


Molgramostim inhalation solution (molgramostim) is an investigational recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in development for the treatment of autoimmune PAP. Molgramostim is delivered via an investigational eFlow® Nebulizer System (PARI Pharma GmbH), specifically developed for inhalation of molgramostim. The safety and efficacy of molgramostim have not been established, and it is not approved by the FDA or any other regulatory authority.


**About Savara**


Savara is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases. Our lead program, molgramostim (molgramostim inhalation solution), is a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in development for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (aPAP). Molgramostim is delivered via a proprietary investigational eFlow® Nebulizer System (PARI Pharma GmbH) specifically developed for inhalation of molgramostim. Our management team has significant experience in rare respiratory diseases and pulmonary medicine, identifying unmet needs, and effectively advancing product candidates to approval and commercialization. More information can be found at[www.savarapharma.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.savarapharma.com&esheet=54644507&newsitemid=20261120300122&lan=en-US&anchor=www.savarapharma.com&index=2&md5=d28478f0c656b94c941ef71a622bfdaf) and[LinkedIn](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fcompany%2Fsavara-pharmaceuticals&esheet=54644507&newsitemid=20261120300122&lan=en-US&anchor=LinkedIn&index=3&md5=f6d5efe9a431a6a8b52ae60b41851dd9) .
